explanations.explanation: The feature detects passages of legal boilerplate—especially the standardized license and warranty disclaimer text (e.g. from Apache or MPL headers) that includes disjunctive phrases like “either express or implied.”

This feature detects and represents standardized legal boilerplate—specifically copyright and license header text (including version numbers, distribution terms, and warranty disclaimers) that typically appears at the beginning of source files.

It appears this feature “lights up” whenever the model encounters a technical‐term fragment—namely a subword like “put” (as in “impli­cit” or “com­put­er”) that commonly occurs within code identifiers, technical comments, and formal/scientific texts. In short, the feature seems to represent the recognition of that “-put” morpheme (and its split‐token variants), flagging parts of words that signal technical or computer‐related language.
